intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Game Drive
experiences.description: Early morning and late afternoon game drives in the Maasai Mara National Reserve, offering the best chance to spot the Big Five. Stay at a camp within or directly adjacent to the reserve to maximize time in the park and avoid long transfers. Since your flight arrives late on Day 1, plan to travel to the Mara on Day 2 and begin drives from Day 3 onwards.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Great Wildebeest Migration River Crossing
experiences.description: Witness the dramatic Mara River crossings where hundreds of thousands of wildebeest brave crocodile-filled waters. Book a camp on the western corridor of the Mara close to the Mara River to eliminate long morning drives and catch crossings as they happen. Ideal between July and October.
experiences.location: Mara River, Western Maasai Mara, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli National Park Elephant Encounter
experiences.description: Spend two days in Amboseli, famous for its large elephant herds set against the backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Stay at a lodge inside or on the boundary of the park to avoid wasting time on road transfers. The late arrival on Day 1 in Nairobi means an early morning drive or short flight to Amboseli on Day 2 is ideal.

experiences.name: Guided Nature Walk with Maasai Warriors
experiences.description: Join a guided bush walk led by local Maasai warriors around the conservancies bordering the Maasai Mara. Learn about medicinal plants, animal tracking, and Maasai culture up close. Staying at a camp within the conservancy means this activity is steps from your accommodation, making it easy to start promptly after breakfast.
experiences.location: Olare Motorogi Conservancy, Maasai Mara, Narok County

experiences.name: Sundowner at the Mara Escarpment
experiences.description: End your safari days with a guided sundowner experience at the Great Rift Valley escarpment overlooking the Maasai Mara ecosystem. Sip local Kenyan wines and snacks while watching the sun set over the savannah. Camps in the Mara typically include this as part of their evening program, keeping costs low and logistics simple.
experiences.location: Oloololo Escarpment, Maasai Mara, Narok County

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a budget shuttle or shared matatu transfer toward Narok County (approximately 3–4 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley escarpment.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Narok County Boutique Stay. Freshen up, explore the immediate surroundings of the guesthouse, and get oriented with the local area. Chat with staff about upcoming safari options and budget tips.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport — budget KES 300–500 at airport kiosks.
meals.lunch: Quick bite at a roadside local eatery along the Nairobi–Narok highway. Try nyama choma (grilled meat) or chapati with beans — budget KES 200–350.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the guesthouse or a nearby local restaurant in Narok town. Try ugali with sukuma wiki (collard greens) and beef stew — budget KES 300–500.

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Kenyan Shillings (KES) handy for road snacks and tips. Shared matatus from Nairobi to Narok cost approximately KES 300–500 and are the most budget-friendly option. Stay hydrated during the drive.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Maasai Mara National Reserve gate area for a budget-friendly game drive. Consider joining a shared group safari vehicle organized through your guesthouse to split costs. Spot lions, elephants, giraffes, and zebras in their natural habitat during the golden morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the game drive through the Mara ecosystem, focusing on the Mara River area where hippos and crocodiles are frequently spotted. Return to the guesthouse by early afternoon for lunch and rest during the warmest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local Narok market to browse Maasai crafts, beaded jewelry, and colorful shukas (blankets). Interact with local Maasai vendors and learn about their culture. Watch a spectacular African sunset over the savannah.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the guesthouse — enjoy mandazi (fried dough) with chai tea — budget KES 150–250.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light meal at the guesthouse — rice and lentil stew — budget KES 200–350.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Narok eatery. Try tilapia fish with ugali and kachumbari (tomato-onion salad) — budget KES 350–500.

day_by_day.notes: Book shared safari vehicles through your guesthouse a day in advance to secure the best group rates. Entry to Maasai Mara costs approximately USD 70–80 per person per day for non-residents — consider a multi-day pass for savings. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket for early morning drives.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day game drive inside Maasai Mara National Reserve. Start at dawn (around 06:00) to catch predators — lions, cheetahs, and leopards — active during the cooler morning hours. Explore the Talek River zone known for big cat sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the open savannah grasslands of the Mara Triangle. Look for the Big Five — lion, leopard, rhino, elephant, and buffalo. July is the beginning of the Great Wildebeest Migration season, so watch for large herds beginning to cross from the Serengeti.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the guesthouse by 18:00. Relax with a cold Tusker beer or fresh passion fruit juice. Share safari stories with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast prepared by the guesthouse — boiled eggs, bread, and fruit — budget KES 150–200.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch inside the reserve at a designated picnic site — packed sandwiches, fruit, and water from the guesthouse — budget KES 200–300.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the guesthouse. Enjoy a hearty plate of pilau rice (spiced rice) with chicken — budget KES 350–500.

day_by_day.notes: July marks the start of the Great Wildebeest Migration — one of the world's greatest wildlife spectacles. Binoculars are highly recommended. Carry at least 2 liters of water per person for the full-day drive. Weather is warm around 25°C with minimal rain — ideal safari conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Maasai village (manyatta) near Narok for an authentic cultural experience. Many villages offer guided tours for a small fee (KES 500–1,000 per person). Learn about Maasai traditions, livestock herding, and traditional medicine from local elders.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Oloolaimutia Gate area of the Mara on a self-guided nature walk with a certified local guide. Spot smaller wildlife — mongoose, dik-dik, warthogs, and a variety of bird species including lilac-breasted rollers and secretary birds.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the guesthouse. Optional: attend a traditional Maasai dance performance if arranged by the guesthouse. Watch the stunning night sky over the savannah — minimal light pollution makes stargazing exceptional.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — porridge (uji) with fresh banana — budget KES 150–200.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Maasai village or a nearby local canteen — traditional githeri (maize and beans) — budget KES 200–300.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple communal meal with fellow travelers at the guesthouse if kitchen facilities are available, or dine at a local restaurant — grilled chicken with chips — budget KES 400–600.

day_by_day.notes: Always ask permission before photographing Maasai community members and offer a small tip if they agree. Local nature walks are far more affordable than full game drives and offer a unique ground-level wildlife perspective. Wear neutral-colored clothing for the walk.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ol Kinyei Conservancy or Naboisho Conservancy — community conservancies adjacent to the Mara that offer more affordable entry fees than the main reserve and less crowded game viewing. Spot elephants, giraffes, and plains game in a tranquil setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided bush walk inside the conservancy with a Maasai ranger. Learn to identify animal tracks, medicinal plants, and bird calls. This immersive experience connects you deeply with the ecosystem beyond the vehicle window.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Narok town by late afternoon. Browse the Narok town center for affordable souvenirs — Maasai beadwork, wooden carvings, and soapstone items. Enjoy the lively local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — fried eggs, toast, and chai — budget KES 150–250.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the guesthouse to enjoy in the conservancy — budget KES 200–300.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a popular local Narok restaurant. Try nyama choma (grilled goat) with ugali and a cold soda — budget KES 400–600.

day_by_day.notes: Community conservancies support local Maasai communities directly — a more ethical and often more affordable alternative to the main reserve. Entry fees are typically USD 30–50 per person. Bush walks must always be conducted with a certified armed ranger for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bird watching session around the guesthouse and nearby wetlands. The Mara ecosystem hosts over 450 bird species. Look for African fish eagles, crowned cranes, flamingos (if near water sources), and numerous raptor species. Bring a bird identification guide or use a free app.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mara River viewpoint for spectacular scenery. During July, wildebeest crossings may already be occurring — one of nature's most dramatic events. Watch from the riverbank as thousands of wildebeest brave crocodile-infested waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography walk near the guesthouse. The warm golden light of the African sunset over the savannah is breathtaking. Capture silhouettes of acacia trees and grazing wildlife.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the guesthouse — fresh fruit salad and yogurt — budget KES 150–200.
meals.lunch: Roadside local canteen near the Mara River — rice and beans with a chapati — budget KES 200–300.
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner — enjoy a warm bowl of vegetable soup with bread — budget KES 250–400.

day_by_day.notes: Bird watching is completely free and one of the most rewarding budget activities in Kenya. The Mara River wildebeest crossings are unpredictable — patience is key. Early morning and late afternoon offer the best photography light. Bring a telephoto lens or a phone with a zoom attachment if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip toward Lake Naivasha (approximately 2.5–3 hours from Narok by matatu via Narok–Naivasha road). Arrive at the lake and take an affordable boat ride to Crescent Island Game Sanctuary — a unique walking safari island where animals roam freely.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk among giraffes, zebras, wildebeest, and waterbuck on Crescent Island without fences or barriers — an extraordinary ground-level wildlife experience. Spot hippos in the lake from the boat. Return to the lake shore by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Lake Naivasha shoreline before heading back to Narok. Watch for African fish eagles diving for fish — a spectacular sight. Return to the guesthouse by evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the guesthouse before departure — mandazi and chai — budget KES 100–200.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Lake Naivasha. Try fresh tilapia from the lake with ugali — budget KES 300–500.
meals.dinner: Late dinner back in Narok — simple rice and stew at a local eatery — budget KES 300–450.

day_by_day.notes: Matatu fare from Narok to Naivasha is approximately KES 300–500 each way. Boat rides to Crescent Island cost approximately KES 1,000–1,500 per person. Walking safari entry is an additional KES 500–800. This is a long day — start early by 07:00. Lake Naivasha is at a higher altitude and can feel cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the guesthouse. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Reflect on your wildlife experiences by journaling or organizing your photos. Chat with the guesthouse staff for insider tips on hidden local gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Narok town on foot. Visit the local open-air market to experience everyday Kenyan life — fresh produce, spices, and livestock trading. Walk along the main street and observe the blend of Maasai and modern Kenyan culture.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local community football (soccer) match if one is happening — a fantastic way to mingle with locals and experience authentic Kenyan community spirit. Football is hugely popular and games are free to watch.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed guesthouse breakfast — full spread of eggs, toast, fruit, and chai — budget KES 200–300.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at the Narok market — mutura (Kenyan sausage), roasted maize, and fresh sugarcane juice — budget KES 150–250.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant in Narok. Try biryani rice with beef and a cold Stoney Tangawizi (ginger soda) — budget KES 350–500.

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are important on longer trips — your body needs recovery time, especially after multiple early morning safari drives. The Narok market is most lively in the morning and early afternoon. Always keep your belongings secure in busy market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Final full game drive in Maasai Mara National Reserve. Focus on areas you haven't yet explored — the Mara Triangle (western sector) offers excellent predator sightings and is often less crowded. Look for cheetah mothers with cubs in July.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mara Elephant Project information center (if accessible) to learn about elephant conservation efforts in the ecosystem. Many conservation organizations offer free or low-cost educational visits that support their funding.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and celebration of your Kenya wildlife adventure. Splurge slightly on a nicer local meal to mark the occasion. Share memories with fellow travelers met along the way.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast for the game drive — boiled eggs, fruit, and thermos of chai — budget KES 150–200.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the reserve at a designated spot — packed from the guesthouse — budget KES 200–300.
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at the best local restaurant in Narok. Try a mixed grill platter with nyama choma, chicken, and sausages with a cold Tusker beer — budget KES 600–900.

day_by_day.notes: Book your final game drive vehicle the evening before to ensure availability. The Mara Triangle is managed separately by the Trans Mara County Council and has a slightly different entry fee structure. Ask your guesthouse for the most current pricing. Take time to tip your safari driver-guide — KES 500–1,000 per day is customary and greatly appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk near the guesthouse — soak in the last views of the Kenyan savannah landscape. Pack your bags and check out of the Narok County Boutique Stay. Exchange any remaining Kenyan Shillings or use them for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a shared matatu or shuttle transfer back to Nairobi (approximately 3–4 hours). Stop at a viewpoint along the Great Rift Valley escarpment for one last panoramic photo of Kenya's stunning landscape. Arrive in Nairobi with time to freshen up before any onward travel.
day_by_day.evening: Spend any remaining time in Nairobi exploring the city center if your flight is late, or head directly to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Kenyan coffee, tea, or crafts as gifts.

meals.breakfast: Final guesthouse breakfast — enjoy a full meal before the journey — budget KES 200–300.
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop en route to Nairobi — nyama choma or a quick chapati wrap — budget KES 200–350.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a quick bite in Nairobi CBD if time allows — Java House or a local café for Kenyan coffee and a snack — budget KES 400–600.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at JKIA. Matatu from Narok to Nairobi costs KES 300–500. Keep your park entry receipts and any wildlife certificates as souvenirs. Declare any wildlife products (even legal crafts) at customs to avoid complications. Kenya's wildlife is unforgettable — consider supporting a conservation charity before you leave.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use pre-arrival time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Nairobi to Narok County (approx. 3–4 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley with views of the escarpment. Check in to Narok County Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation walk around the property grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in with a welcome sundowner drink at the lodge. Enjoy a casual dinner at the boutique stay's in-house restaurant. Early night to prepare for full safari days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Quick stop at a roadside café or petrol station canteen in Naivasha along the transfer route — try a simple nyama choma (grilled meat) wrap or samosas (approx. KES 500–800)
meals.dinner: In-house restaurant at Narok County Boutique Stay — enjoy a set Kenyan dinner menu featuring ugali, sukuma wiki, and grilled chicken or beef stew (approx. KES 1,500–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light and accessible for the road transfer. Exchange currency at the Nairobi airport forex bureau before departing. Carry snacks and water for the drive. July is peak migration season — the lodge may be busy, so confirm your reservation upon landing.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Maasai Mara Game Drive departing at 06:00. Head into the Maasai Mara National Reserve at dawn for the best big cat sightings — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are most active at this hour. Look out for the Big Five across the golden savannah grasslands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge by 10:30 for a late bush breakfast. After a short rest, embark on an afternoon game drive re-entering the reserve around 15:30 to catch predators on the hunt and large herbivore herds grazing before dusk.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the Mara Escarpment — join a guided sundowner experience at the Great Rift Valley escarpment overlook with drinks and light snacks as the sun dips below the horizon. Return to lodge for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field or back at the lodge — packed box with boiled eggs, fruit, bread, and coffee/tea (included with game drive package)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge — fresh salad, sandwiches, and fruit juice (approx. KES 1,200–1,800)
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant dinner — three-course meal with Kenyan-inspired dishes such as tilapia fish, lentil soup, and seasonal vegetables (approx. KES 2,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored, layered clothing — mornings in July can be cool (15–18°C) before warming to 25°C by midday. Bring binoculars and a fully charged camera. Book game drives through the lodge for mid-range pricing (approx. USD 60–90 per person per drive).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive at 06:00 focusing on the Mara River zone — position near crossing points to maximize chances of witnessing wildebeest activity. July is the height of the Great Migration, making river crossings highly likely.
day_by_day.afternoon: Great Wildebeest Migration River Crossing experience — spend the afternoon stationed at a prime Mara River crossing point with a guide. Watch hundreds of thousands of wildebeest and zebras brave crocodile-filled waters in one of nature's most dramatic spectacles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a communal campfire at the lodge with fellow travelers, sharing the day's sightings. Light dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the lodge before departure — thermos coffee, muffins, and fruit
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the field prepared by the lodge — sandwiches, boiled eggs, juice, and fresh fruit (included in full-day excursion package)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the lodge — wood-fired flatbread, bean stew, grilled vegetables, and Kenyan chai (approx. KES 1,800–2,500)

day_by_day.notes: River crossings cannot be guaranteed as they depend on wildebeest movement, but July–August is statistically the peak period. Be patient and stay quiet at the riverbank. Full-day excursion packages including lunch are available from most lodges at approx. USD 100–130 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Guided Nature Walk with Maasai Warriors — depart at 07:30 for a 3-hour guided bush walk led by local Maasai warriors in the conservancies bordering the Maasai Mara. Learn to track wildlife on foot, identify medicinal plants, and hear stories about Maasai culture and their coexistence with wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai village (manyatta) near the conservancy for a cultural exchange — see traditional homesteads, watch a jumping ceremony (adumu), and browse handcrafted beadwork and souvenirs. Support local artisans directly.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the Mara Escarpment for a second visit — this time with a focus on the sweeping Rift Valley panorama at golden hour. Return to lodge for dinner and a night-sky stargazing session if weather permits.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the lodge before the walk — eggs, toast, porridge, fresh juice, and tea/coffee (approx. KES 1,000–1,500 or included in stay)
meals.lunch: Light lunch back at the lodge after the walk — grilled tilapia or chicken with rice and salad (approx. KES 1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — Kenyan beef stew with ugali, kachumbari salad, and fresh passion fruit juice (approx. KES 2,000–2,800)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for the bush walk. Maasai warrior guides are highly knowledgeable — tip them directly (KES 500–1,000 per person is appreciated). Village entry fees are typically USD 20–30 per person. Purchase crafts directly from artisans to ensure fair compensation.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the lodge — sleep in slightly and enjoy a relaxed breakfast. Take a gentle walk around the lodge gardens, do some birdwatching from the veranda (over 450 bird species recorded in the Mara ecosystem), and review your wildlife photographs from the week so far.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive (15:30–18:30) with a specific focus on birdlife and smaller mammals — mongoose, bat-eared foxes, servals, and diverse raptors. A change of pace from big game hunting, offering new photographic opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Communal sundowner at the lodge's outdoor terrace. Enjoy a special mid-trip dinner at the lodge's upgraded dining experience — a slightly elevated menu to mark the halfway point of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the lodge — full spread with fresh fruit, eggs to order, toast, and Kenyan tea (approx. KES 1,200–1,800 or included)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the lodge — avocado toast, fruit salad, and fresh lemonade (approx. KES 800–1,200)
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated lodge dinner — grilled Nile perch, roasted sweet potatoes, seasonal greens, and a local Tusker beer or fresh juice (approx. KES 2,500–3,500)

day_by_day.notes: This is a lighter activity day — use it to recharge physically and mentally. July weather in the Mara is warm (25°C highs) with minimal rain (30mm for the month), making outdoor relaxation very comfortable. Carry sunscreen and a hat for afternoon activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive at 06:00 with a dedicated focus on lion prides and cheetah families — July is an excellent month for big cat sightings as prey is abundant due to the migration. Request a guide specializing in predator tracking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge by 10:30. After lunch and rest, take a self-guided nature trail around the lodge's private conservancy land (if available) or relax by the lodge pool/lounge area. Pack bags lightly for the next day's transfer to Amboseli.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sundowner at the Mara Escarpment for a final Rift Valley view. Return to lodge for a final Narok County dinner and early night ahead of the Amboseli transfer.

meals.breakfast: Packed field breakfast — thermos coffee, boiled eggs, banana, and granola bar
meals.lunch: Lodge lunch — pasta or rice dish with grilled vegetables and fresh juice (approx. KES 1,500–2,000)
meals.dinner: Final lodge dinner in Narok — mixed grill platter with nyama choma, chicken, and roasted corn with chapati and kachumbari (approx. KES 2,000–3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the Amboseli transfer logistics with the lodge today — arrange a shared shuttle or private transfer departing the next morning. The drive from Narok County to Amboseli is approximately 5–6 hours via Nairobi or the southern route. Book ahead to secure mid-range transport (approx. USD 40–70 per person for shared shuttle).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Narok County Boutique Stay at 07:00 for the transfer to Amboseli National Park (approx. 5–6 hours). Enjoy the changing landscapes — from Mara grasslands to the dramatic views of Mount Kilimanjaro appearing on the horizon as you approach Amboseli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Amboseli area by early afternoon. Check in to your mid-range Amboseli accommodation (arrange in advance — options include Amboseli Sopa Lodge or Ol Tukai Lodge at approx. USD 150–200 per night). Freshen up and take a short late-afternoon game drive (15:30–18:00) to get oriented in the park.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the lodge with views of Mount Kilimanjaro at dusk — on a clear July evening, the snow-capped peak is spectacularly visible. Dinner at the lodge restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Narok County Boutique Stay before departure — toast, fruit, and coffee (included in stay)
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route — try a local town restaurant in Emali or Sultan Hamud for a simple Kenyan lunch of rice, beans, and chapati (approx. KES 400–700)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amboseli lodge restaurant — buffet-style Kenyan and international dishes (approx. KES 2,500–3,500 or included in full-board package)

day_by_day.notes: The transfer day is long — bring snacks, water, a book, and entertainment. Roads between Narok and Amboseli vary in quality; some sections may be unpaved. July is dry season in Amboseli, offering excellent visibility and dusty but photogenic conditions around the swamps.

day_by_day.morning: Amboseli National Park Elephant Encounter — full morning game drive (06:00–10:30) specifically focused on Amboseli's famous large elephant herds. The park is home to some of Africa's largest tuskers. Photograph elephants with the iconic snow-capped Kilimanjaro backdrop — one of Africa's most iconic wildlife images.
day_by_day.afternoon: Midday rest at the lodge during the hottest hours. After lunch, join a 15:30 afternoon game drive focusing on the Amboseli swamps — home to hippos, cape buffalo, and diverse waterbirds including pelicans, herons, and crowned cranes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge for sundowner drinks on the terrace with Kilimanjaro views. Dinner at the lodge followed by an optional guided night walk or spotlight drive (if offered by the lodge at approx. USD 30–40 per person).

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast before the morning drive — thermos coffee, pastries, and fruit
meals.lunch: Full lunch at the lodge — soup, main course, and dessert (included in full-board or approx. KES 2,000–2,800 à la carte)
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner — three-course meal with Kenyan and continental options; try the Amboseli tilapia if available (approx. KES 2,500–3,500 or full-board)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is dustier than the Mara — bring a buff/scarf to protect against dust on game drives. Elephant encounters here are remarkably close and intimate; maintain respectful distances. The Amboseli Elephant Research Project has been running since 1972 — ask your guide about individual elephant family histories.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning game drive in Amboseli (06:00–10:00) — a last chance to observe elephants, lions, and the stunning Kilimanjaro backdrop. Focus on photography and quiet observation. Visit the Observation Hill viewpoint for a panoramic overview of the entire Amboseli basin and swamp system.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge for checkout and begin the transfer back toward Nairobi (approx. 4 hours). If time permits, stop at the Chyulu Hills viewpoint en route for a final scenic landscape photograph. Arrive in Nairobi by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a mid-range Nairobi hotel for the final night (options: Nairobi Serena Hotel or Ole Sereni at approx. USD 100–150 per night). Enjoy a celebratory farewell dinner at a Nairobi restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast in Amboseli — full cooked breakfast with eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the lodge for the road — sandwiches, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a Nairobi restaurant — try Carnivore Restaurant (famous for its nyama choma experience, approx. USD 35–45 per person) or Talisman Restaurant in Karen for upscale Kenyan cuisine (approx. USD 30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Nairobi–Amboseli road can have variable traffic — depart by 13:00 to avoid evening Nairobi traffic. Store valuables securely in Nairobi. If interested in a final souvenir shopping stop, the Maasai Market operates on rotating days around Nairobi — check the schedule in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed final morning in Nairobi. Visit the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage in Nairobi National Park (open 11:00–12:00 daily, entry approx. USD 7 per person) — a perfect wildlife farewell featuring baby elephant feeding and keeper talks. Alternatively, visit the Giraffe Centre in Karen (entry approx. USD 15 per person) for close-up giraffe feeding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping at the Kazuri Beads Workshop in Karen or the Utamaduni Craft Centre — both offer authentic, fairly traded Kenyan crafts at mid-range prices. Head to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for departure check-in (allow 3 hours before flight).
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure lounge — relax with a final Kenyan coffee and reflect on 10 extraordinary days of wildlife and nature. Board your return flight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Nairobi — full buffet with fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and Kenyan tea/coffee (included in hotel stay or approx. KES 1,500–2,000)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in the Karen area after morning activities — try Tamambo Karen Blixen Café for a relaxed garden setting with sandwiches and salads (approx. KES 1,500–2,500)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or lounge — international options available at JKIA (approx. KES 1,500–2,500); alternatively, bring snacks from the city

day_by_day.notes: JKIA is approximately 20–30 minutes from central Nairobi but allow extra time for traffic. Declare any wildlife products, wooden items, or cultural artifacts at customs if required. Ensure your yellow fever vaccination certificate is accessible as it may be checked on departure. Kenya Wildlife Service conservation fees paid during the trip contribute directly to wildlife protection — a meaningful contribution to the ecosystems you experienced.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Game Drive
experiences.description: Early morning and late afternoon game drives in the Maasai Mara National Reserve, offering the best chance to spot the Big Five. Stay at a camp within or directly adjacent to the reserve to maximize time in the park and avoid long transfers. Since your flight arrives late on Day 1, plan to travel to the Mara on Day 2 and begin drives from Day 3 onwards.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Great Wildebeest Migration River Crossing
experiences.description: Witness the dramatic Mara River crossings where hundreds of thousands of wildebeest brave crocodile-filled waters. Book a camp on the western corridor of the Mara close to the Mara River to eliminate long morning drives and catch crossings as they happen. Ideal between July and October.
experiences.location: Mara River, Western Maasai Mara, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli National Park Elephant Encounter
experiences.description: Spend two days in Amboseli, famous for its large elephant herds set against the backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Stay at a lodge inside or on the boundary of the park to avoid wasting time on road transfers. The late arrival on Day 1 in Nairobi means an early morning drive or short flight to Amboseli on Day 2 is ideal.

experiences.name: Guided Nature Walk with Maasai Warriors
experiences.description: Join a guided bush walk led by local Maasai warriors around the conservancies bordering the Maasai Mara. Learn about medicinal plants, animal tracking, and Maasai culture up close. Staying at a camp within the conservancy means this activity is steps from your accommodation, making it easy to start promptly after breakfast.
experiences.location: Olare Motorogi Conservancy, Maasai Mara, Narok County

experiences.name: Sundowner at the Mara Escarpment
experiences.description: End your safari days with a guided sundowner experience at the Great Rift Valley escarpment overlooking the Maasai Mara ecosystem. Sip local Kenyan wines and snacks while watching the sun set over the savannah. Camps in the Mara typically include this as part of their evening program, keeping costs low and logistics simple.
experiences.location: Oloololo Escarpment, Maasai Mara, Narok County

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 13:00 on flight LH. No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Nairobi to Narok County Boutique Stay (approximately 3–4 hours via the scenic Rift Valley route).
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive through the Great Rift Valley en route to Narok County. Stop at a Rift Valley viewpoint for photographs and refreshments provided by your private driver-guide. Arrive at the Narok County Boutique Stay, check in, and settle into your luxury suite. Enjoy a welcome orientation with your personal safari concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed welcome dinner at the boutique stay's private dining terrace under the stars. Briefing with your lead guide about the days ahead, wildlife expectations, and safety protocols.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and snacks provided during the private transfer — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages from a curated hamper
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the Narok County Boutique Stay — three-course set menu featuring Kenyan-inspired cuisine: roasted Maasai lamb, seasonal vegetables, and a selection of East African wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrival transfer should be pre-arranged with a luxury ground operator. Confirm luggage weight limits for any light aircraft legs later in the trip. Keep the first evening low-key to recover from travel fatigue. Weather expected warm at ~25°C.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise at 05:30 for a pre-dawn breakfast before heading out on your first Maasai Mara Game Drive. Depart by 06:00 in a customized 4x4 Land Cruiser with a private KPSGA-certified guide. Focus on the Big Five during the golden morning light — lions are particularly active at this hour on the Mara plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the boutique stay for a gourmet bush brunch. After a short rest, embark on an afternoon game drive from 16:00, exploring the open savannah grasslands and riverine forests. Look for leopards in the fig trees and large elephant breeding herds near the Mara River tributaries.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the Mara Escarpment — a guided experience at the Great Rift Valley escarpment overlook with panoramic views across the Mara. Enjoy chilled champagne, canapés, and the spectacle of the African sunset painting the sky in burnt oranges and purples.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn continental breakfast at the lodge — fresh pastries, tropical fruits, yogurt, and Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush brunch on the lodge terrace — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh salads, and tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at the boutique stay — pan-seared Nile perch, roasted root vegetables, and a curated Kenyan cheese board with local honey

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral, earth-toned clothing for game drives. Bring binoculars, a camera with a telephoto lens, and sunscreen. July is peak season for the Great Wildebeest Migration — herds are likely already gathering near the Mara River.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive departing at 06:00, this time venturing specifically toward the Mara River crossings zone. Position near a known crossing point with your expert guide to maximize the chance of witnessing the Great Wildebeest Migration River Crossing — one of the most dramatic wildlife spectacles on Earth. Hundreds of thousands of wildebeest brave the crocodile-infested waters in frenzied surges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for lunch and an afternoon rest during the midday heat. Optional: visit the boutique stay's spa for a traditional Maasai-inspired massage using locally sourced oils and herbs. Alternatively, enjoy a curated wildlife documentary screening in the lodge's media lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Private sundowner in the bush — your guide will set up a bespoke outdoor bar at a scenic location within the conservancy. Gin and tonics, wine, and artisan canapés as the savannah settles into twilight. Night drive back to the lodge spotting nocturnal species.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field — thermos coffee, freshly baked muffins, boiled eggs, and seasonal fruits enjoyed with a view of the Mara plains
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the lodge — grilled chicken wraps, avocado salad, fresh lemonade, and chilled gazpacho
meals.dinner: Private dining experience — slow-braised beef short rib with Kenyan spices, ugali, sukuma wiki, and a selection of South African Cabernet Sauvignon

day_by_day.notes: The Mara River crossings are unpredictable — patience is essential. Your guide will monitor radio communications with other guides to find active crossing points. Bring a dust cover for camera equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Guided Nature Walk with Maasai Warriors departing at 07:00. Join an immersive bush walk led by two experienced Maasai warrior guides through the conservancies bordering the Maasai Mara. Learn to track wildlife on foot, identify medicinal plants, read animal spoor, and understand the Maasai's deep relationship with the land. Encounter zebra, giraffe, and buffalo at close range on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge by 11:00. Enjoy a leisurely lunch followed by a cultural visit to a traditional Maasai boma (village) near the conservancy. Participate in traditional dances, learn about Maasai customs, beadwork, and pastoralist lifestyle. Purchase authentic handcrafted jewelry and artifacts directly from artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the boutique stay. Enjoy cocktails at the lodge bar — try a Dawa (Swahili for 'medicine'), Kenya's iconic honey-vodka-lime cocktail. Dinner under the open sky on the lodge's fire-lit terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full English-style safari breakfast at the lodge — eggs to order, grilled tomatoes, Kenyan sausages, toast, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Mezze-style lunch on the lodge veranda — hummus, grilled flatbreads, roasted vegetables, and marinated chicken skewers
meals.dinner: Fire-pit dinner on the lodge terrace — whole roasted lamb (nyama choma style), grilled corn, kachumbari salad, and malva pudding for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes for the bush walk. The Maasai cultural visit fee often directly supports community conservation programs — confirm with the lodge that a community benefit contribution is included. Bring small denomination Kenyan shillings for artisan purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Maasai Mara Game Drive experience — depart at 06:00 for an extended game drive covering the northern Mara Triangle, a less-trafficked zone with exceptional lion pride activity. Your guide will seek out cheetah on the open plains — July is a prime month for cheetah sightings as they hunt Thomson's gazelle fawns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Bush picnic lunch served in the field by your guide and a support vehicle — set up under an acacia tree with folding tables, linen, and a full picnic spread. Continue afternoon game drive exploring the Mara River corridor for hippo pods and Nile crocodiles basking on the banks.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at the Mara Escarpment for a second visit — this time with a private telescope set up for stargazing as dusk falls. Kenya's low light pollution makes for extraordinary night-sky viewing. Return to the lodge for a nightcap and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the lodge before departure — yogurt parfait, granola, tropical fruits, and Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet bush picnic — cold cuts, artisan cheeses, baguettes, quinoa salad, sparkling water, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Chef's tasting menu at the boutique stay — five-course dinner showcasing locally sourced Kenyan ingredients paired with curated East African wines

day_by_day.notes: Request a full-day game drive vehicle with a pop-up roof for optimal photography. Carry sufficient water (at least 2 liters per person). Apply high-SPF sunscreen and wear a wide-brimmed hat during midday hours.

day_by_day.morning: Second Great Wildebeest Migration River Crossing experience — depart early at 05:45 to secure a prime riverside position before other vehicles arrive. The Mara River crossings during July are at their most intense, with multiple crossings possible in a single morning. Your guide will brief you on crocodile behavior and wildebeest herd dynamics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge by midday. Afternoon at leisure — optional hot air balloon safari briefing for tomorrow's experience. Alternatively, enjoy a guided birdwatching session within the lodge grounds and surrounding conservancy, spotting lilac-breasted rollers, secretary birds, and African fish eagles.
day_by_day.evening: Private romantic dinner set up in the bush — your lodge team creates a bespoke candlelit table in a cleared clearing with lanterns, floral arrangements, and a personal chef. A truly unforgettable luxury experience under the Milky Way.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast consumed in the vehicle en route to the river — thermos coffee, pastries, and energy bars
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the lodge — Caesar salad, grilled tilapia, fresh bread, and tropical fruit sorbet
meals.dinner: Exclusive bush dinner — lobster thermidor, grilled vegetables, truffle risotto, and a decadent chocolate fondant with Kenyan vanilla ice cream; paired with premium Champagne

day_by_day.notes: The private bush dinner must be arranged 24 hours in advance with the lodge concierge. Confirm dietary requirements. Bring an extra layer for the evening as temperatures can drop to around 15°C after dark in July.

day_by_day.morning: Hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara — depart the lodge at 05:00 for a pre-dawn transfer to the balloon launch site. Soar silently over the endless plains at sunrise, watching wildebeest herds move below, lions returning from night hunts, and the Mara River glinting in the morning light. Approximately 60–90 minutes of flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional champagne breakfast in the bush following the balloon landing — a hallmark of the Kenyan balloon safari experience. Return to the lodge by midday. Afternoon game drive focusing on the Oloololo escarpment area for leopard and serval sightings.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in the Mara — a guided sundowner walk through the conservancy with your Maasai warrior guides, concluding with drinks around a traditional campfire. Share stories and reflections on the week's wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast post-balloon landing — full cooked breakfast with eggs, bacon, sausages, grilled tomatoes, fresh fruits, and sparkling wine in the field
meals.lunch: Lodge terrace lunch — butternut squash soup, grilled chicken salad, and freshly baked bread
meals.dinner: Campfire dinner under the stars — traditional Kenyan stew (mchuzi wa nyama), pilau rice, chapati, and a decadent passion fruit cheesecake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon safaris must be booked well in advance — confirm with the lodge at least 3–4 days prior. Weight limits apply (typically 100–110 kg per passenger). The balloon experience is weather-dependent and may be rescheduled if conditions are unsafe.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Narok County by private vehicle or chartered light aircraft for Amboseli National Park (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 1 hour by charter flight). En route, enjoy the changing landscapes from Mara savannah to semi-arid Amboseli plains. Arrive at your Amboseli luxury camp by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Amboseli National Park Elephant Encounter begins — afternoon game drive in Amboseli, home to Africa's largest and most studied elephant herds. The iconic backdrop of snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895m) creates one of Africa's most photogenic wildlife settings. Observe matriarchal elephant families at close range with expert interpretation from your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the lodge deck with Mount Kilimanjaro turning pink and purple at dusk — a world-class photographic opportunity. Dinner at the Amboseli lodge's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Narok boutique stay before departure — eggs, toast, fresh fruit, and Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box for the transfer — sandwiches, fresh fruit, chocolate brownie, and chilled drinks
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Amboseli luxury lodge — slow-cooked Amboseli-style goat curry, steamed basmati rice, roasted vegetables, and a selection of Kenyan craft beers and wines

day_by_day.notes: If traveling by road, the journey passes through Nairobi — allow extra time for city traffic. A chartered light aircraft from Mara to Amboseli is strongly recommended for comfort and time efficiency. Confirm accommodation at Amboseli separately as this is a different property from the Narok boutique stay.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Amboseli National Park Elephant Encounter — depart at 06:00 for a morning game drive with Mount Kilimanjaro as the backdrop. Amboseli's open plains offer exceptional visibility. Track large elephant bulls with impressive tusks, observe hippos in the Amboseli swamps, and look for lions and cheetah on the open flats. Your guide will share insights from the Amboseli Elephant Research Project, the world's longest-running elephant study.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for lunch and rest. Optional: visit the Amboseli Maasai cultural center for insights into how local communities coexist with wildlife. Alternatively, enjoy a guided nature walk on the lodge's private conservancy, spotting birds and smaller mammals.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Amboseli sundowner — drinks on the lodge's elevated viewing platform as the last light fades over Kilimanjaro. A private chef prepares a special farewell dinner celebrating the highlights of your Kenyan journey.

meals.breakfast: Bush breakfast served in the field near a swamp — thermos coffee, fresh pastries, boiled eggs, and seasonal fruits with elephant herds visible in the distance
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the lodge — grilled Nile perch tacos, mango salsa, sweet potato fries, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at the Amboseli lodge — four-course menu: wild mushroom velouté, Kenyan lobster bisque, grilled beef tenderloin with truffle jus, and a Kilimanjaro-inspired white chocolate and coconut dessert; paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: July mornings in Amboseli can be misty, which creates ethereal photographic conditions with Kilimanjaro emerging from the clouds. Keep your camera ready at all times. The mountain is most visible in the early morning before cloud build-up.

day_by_day.morning: Final early morning game drive in Amboseli at 06:00 — a last opportunity to photograph elephants against Kilimanjaro in the golden morning light. Return to the lodge by 09:00 for a leisurely checkout breakfast. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Amboseli to Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (approximately 4 hours by road or 1 hour by charter flight). En route, stop at a curated Nairobi luxury shopping destination — Karen Blixen Museum area or the Village Market — for last-minute premium Kenyan souvenirs: artisan jewelry, Maasai beadwork, coffee, and wildlife photography books.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nairobi. Access the airport's premium lounge for final refreshments before your flight. Carry memories of the wildebeest crossing, elephant herds beneath Kilimanjaro, Maasai warriors, and spectacular Kenyan sunsets.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely checkout breakfast at the Amboseli lodge — full buffet spread with eggs to order, tropical fruits, pastries, smoked salmon, and premium Kenyan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a recommended Nairobi restaurant en route to the airport — Talisman Restaurant in Karen or Carnivore for a quintessential Kenyan dining experience
meals.dinner: Airport premium lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for check-in and security at JKIA. Confirm excess baggage allowances if you have purchased large souvenirs or additional luggage. Declare any wildlife products (e.g., ivory, certain skins) — purchase only certified legal crafts. Ensure your travel insurance covers the full trip duration.
